intent: The menu popup, portalled and placed at the point where its ContextMenu was opened, holding the menu's rows.
typical_uses: The one popup of a ContextMenu, listing its items, groups, separators and submenus

dont_use_when.situation: A floating panel with fields or buttons the user has to operate
The list of options of a form select
The popup of a nested submenu

invariants.text: The popup is in the DOM only while the menu is open or animating closed; the kit passes no `keepMounted` to the portal, so a closed menu renders nothing.

Without `container`, the popup portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the popup only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.

The popup is placed against the point where the menu was opened, not against the trigger's box, so it takes no width from the trigger; context-menu.module.css gives it a 9rem minimum width and lets it grow with its longest row.
The popup's height is capped at the space the positioner reports as available, and its rows scroll vertically beyond that.

Arrow keys move focus through the items in order, disabled items included, and wrap from the last back to the first unless the root's `loopFocus` is false; typing moves focus to the next item whose text starts with the typed characters.
The popup fades and scales on open and close; under `prefers-reduced-motion` context-menu.module.css drops the transform transition and keeps the fade.

anti_patterns.dont: Keep the default positioning when the trigger sits inside a transformed or filtered container, such as an animated panel
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `positionMethod="fixed"`; absolute positioning resolves against the transformed container instead of the page and misplaces the popup

a11y.by: context-menu.test.tsx asserts that a right click on the trigger renders an element with role menu and that Escape pressed on that menu removes it; the primitive's Menu.Popup keeps focus inside the menu while it is open

children.states: children is the popup's rows, the parts listed under accepts
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the popup portals into; null and undefined both mean no container of its own
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers. The kit resolves it as `container ?? <the enclosing content's container>`, so an explicit null falls through like an absent prop.

sideOffset.states: sideOffset is the gap in pixels between the anchor and the popup, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
sideOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

alignOffset.states: alignOffset is the shift in pixels along the alignment axis, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
alignOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

collisionBoundary.states: collisionBoundary is the area the popup is kept inside, `clipping-ancestors`, an element, a list of elements or a rectangle
collisionBoundary.because: `'clipping-ancestors' | Element | Element[] | Rect` mixes a string with live DOM elements, which no JSON Schema type covers.

collisionPadding.states: collisionPadding is the space in pixels kept from the collision boundary, one number or a per-side object
collisionPadding.because: `number | { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

finalFocus.states: finalFocus decides where focus goes when the popup closes - true for the default, false for nowhere, a ref, or a function of the interaction type
finalFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` mixes a boolean with a ref object and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the popup's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the popup's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, side, align, nested, instant, transitionStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through context-menu.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside ContextMenuContent; only its `container` is exposed, as a prop of the content itself.
Composed inside ContextMenuContent; its placement and collision props are exposed on the content itself.

good.title: A popup with a labelled group and a destructive action
A popup portalled into a themed subtree

bad.title: Content with no ContextMenu root around it
bad.why: The primitive's Portal and Popup read the nearest ContextMenu root's state through context and throw when there is none.
